az_genetic_wall.blurb: A small, little-visited cluster of dark red fins and buttresses on West Twin Butte in the Sedona area, sitting below Devils Thumb. Ten routes, mostly traditional with two hard sport lines, spread from the 5.7 range to the low 5.12s, with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.10 band. The cracks make it a decent place to build crack-climbing skills, since the grades step up gradually from easy warm-ups to a few serious leads. Rock quality is generally good, the views are pleasant, and you are unlikely to find a crowd. Bring a standard trad rack with extra mid-size cams for the wider cracks.

az_flying_buttress.blurb: A long sandstone buttress on the Mitten Ridge side of Sedona, beyond Moose's Butte along Schnebly Hill Road. This is a serious multi-pitch objective rather than a quick cragging stop: seven of the ten routes are trad, two are aid, and one is sport. Free grades run from an easy 5.7 up through a cluster of 5.10 and 5.11 leads to one very hard 5.13. Expect big corners, a huge roof on the west face and an approach under large cliffs. Some lines are run out or have sandy holds and loose rock, so it suits experienced parties with a full rack and an early start.

az_2_broken_symmetry.blurb: A compact bouldering zone high in Middle Elden canyon on Mount Elden above Flagstaff, reached by continuing up the canyon beyond the Skeletor boulders. Ten problems run from around V3 to V12, so there is something for solid boulderers but the area leans toward the hard end, with several at V6 and above. The lowest boulder holds the namesake line and the rest sit up and around the corner. It is a good place to spend a session thanks to some morning shade, and a few pads and a spotter help since landings in this canyon can be rough.

az_floor_pie_roof_flying_saucer.blurb: Two roof boulders on the limestone side of Priest Draw, southeast of Flagstaff, about five minutes up the main trail. Floor Pie Roof is a fully horizontal ceiling with powerful, funky and technical moves, while Flying Saucer is a shorter roof just to its left with plenty of features. Ten problems range from V3 up to V10, with a spread of mid-grade lines and several hard test pieces on the big roof. Because the roofs are sheltered, the rock can stay dry when other spots in the draw are damp. Bring pads and strong fingers.

az_coffin_roof.blurb: A quiet limestone roof tucked among trees on the left side of Priest Draw near Flagstaff, a couple of minutes' walk up the hill from the Island. The namesake attraction is a hidden problem starting from a big coffin-shaped hueco. Ten boulder problems cover V1 through V8, with most falling between V3 and V4, so it works for intermediate boulderers and has a few tougher options. Few people come here, which makes it a peaceful alternative to the busier roofs in the draw.

az_block_the.blurb: A small cluster of boulders in the Lake Mary area south of Flagstaff, tucked beside the main leaning-pillar zone near Lakeview Campground. Ten problems have been established, mostly easy to moderate from V0 to V4, with V3 the most common grade, and there is room for more development. Many lines begin from odd, low positions with only a few footholds. The boulders are a short walk along an elk trail from the pillars, and spring vegetation can hide them, so it is best saved for a lower-key day with a pad or two.

az_back_walls_the.blurb: A sport-climbing sector deep in Lime Kiln Canyon, just east of Mesquite on the Arizona side of the line. It sits farther up the canyon than the two main crags, a further five to ten minutes of walking past them. The grey limestone is mostly vertical to slightly slabby. Ten bolted routes span roughly 5.8 to 5.12, with a few moderates, three in the 5.11 range and three in the 5.12 range, so it suits a group with mixed abilities. Fall and spring are the best seasons in the canyon; winter is cold and summer is hot.

az_lower_flailing_wall.blurb: A small section of the Bright Angel Walls on the Grand Canyon rim, just below the Wailing Wall. Two faces split by a prominent chimney hold ten routes, six sport and four trad, ranging from 5.9 to 5.12 with most at 5.10 and 5.11. The rock is decent for the canyon, though loose pieces near the top call for care. Routes are short, so it works best as a quick workout rather than a full day. Many parties reach the top by traversing from the Wailing Wall and rigging top ropes from the existing anchors.
